question: Should Crabline fail closed on pre-existing artifact directories owned by another POSIX user, or provide a narrowly authorized migration and recovery path for upgrades?
rationale: Rejecting foreign ownership strengthens the security boundary, but legitimate existing stores may have been created by root, containers, or a previous runtime user; the acceptable recovery policy requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Add explicit recovery
options.body: Provide a narrow operator-confirmed recovery or migration flow while retaining strict ownership validation during normal access.

options.title: Accept fail-closed upgrade
options.body: Keep unconditional rejection and document the exact breaking upgrade behavior and required operator migration procedure.

recommendation.title: Add explicit recovery
recommendation.body: Provide a narrow operator-confirmed recovery or migration flow while retaining strict ownership validation during normal access.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Crabline OpenClaw bridge and channel-foundation history makes this person the best available owner for the upgrade-contract decision.
